title: stream-pool-token-prefetch-and-adaptive-retry-presets-across-sdks
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Reduce cold-starts for token refresh during high-concurrency streaming workloads and bring a consistent ergonomic streaming surface across Python/TS/Go SDKs. This PR introduces a lightweight per-client stream pool + transient token prefetcher, adds adaptive retry presets tuned for streaming vs. unary workloads, and performs minor API ergonomics to simplify common patterns.

What changed (high level):
- SDK core: introduce StreamPool abstraction (client-local, lock-free-ish pool of stream handles) with optional credential prefetch hooks.
- Auth: add transient_token_prefetch option that proactively refreshes short-lived credentials when pool size grows to prevent mid-stream reauth stalls. Works with existing token providers.
- Retries: add adaptive_retry_profile setting with presets: "unary-fast", "stream-stable", "stream-low-latency". Presets tune backoff windows and max-retries to match streaming semantics.
- Ergonomics: expose new StreamHandle.async_iter() in Python, a Symbol.asyncIterator-friendly facade in TypeScript, and a StreamHandle.Consume(ctx) convenience helper in Go. All three aim for single-call consumption patterns.
- Version bumps: python -> 0.14.0, typescript -> 2.7.0, go -> v1.10.1; changelogs updated.
- Tests & docs: unit and integration tests added for prefetch race conditions; updated quickstarts and a migration note in SDK migration guide.

Checklist:
- [x] API design review with SDK leads
- [x] Cross-language behavior tests
- [x] Performance microbenchmarks for concurrent streaming
- [x] Telemetry hooks for pool metrics

Backward compatibility / migration notes:
- Default behavior unchanged unless users opt into stream_pool or transient_token_prefetch. Migration guide includes minimal code snippets to opt in.
- Some internal method names in StreamHandle were renamed; these were previously undocumented and should not impact public users.

Related: ENG-13579 (stream stability), PM-2468 (SDK ergonomics initiative).

Detailed changes: see files_changed and commits for granular diffs. This description intentionally stays high level.

chore(sdk): expose ergonomic stream consumption helpers across languages
test: add concurrency/fuzz tests for pool and prefetch races
docs: migration guide + changelog bumps for py/ts/go
ci: add benchmark job for concurrent streams
review_comments: Marco Li: Can we signal when a prefetched token fails mid-stream so the consumer can retry gracefully? Suggest adding an on_prefetch_failure callback.
Aisha Patel: Added on_prefetch_failure and wired it through the Python/TS APIs. Default handler emits telemetry and attempts one inline refresh; documented the behavior.
Sven Müller: The Go helper Consume(ctx) looks convenient but hides cancellation semantics. Please add examples showing context cancellation and emphasize cancellation propagation in docs.
Aisha Patel: Expanded Go docs and added an explicit Cancel() example in stream_handle.go comments and migration doc.
Hannah Ortiz: CI bench job flaked once; re-run showed stable results but please include benchmark numbers in PR description for record.

Aisha Patel: Pasted benchmark summary into the PR thread and CI artifact link. microbench: 10k concurrent short streams increased median p50 by 8ms vs baseline, tail (p99) reduced by 22% when prefetch enabled with pool size 8.
release_notes: Introduce StreamPool and transient_token_prefetch across SDKs; add adaptive retry presets for streaming workloads; expose ergonomic stream consumption helpers; version bumps: python 0.14.0, typescript 2.7.0, go v1.10.1.
